title: scValToNative and humanizeEvents drop the ScErrorType of every non-contract error

target.versions_affected: 16.3.0 - 17.4.0 (executed by the kit on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 16.4.1, 17.2.0, 17.2.1, 17.3.0 and 17.4.0) and master 5243062 (since stellar/js-stellar-base#753; lower bound not established)

severity_basis: scvError values of every type other than sceContract become { type: "system", code, value } with only the ScErrorCode, so Error(Storage, ExceededLimit) and Error(Budget, ExceededLimit) are indistinguishable; humanizeEvents runs scValToNative on each diagnostic topic, so the failure reason of a failed Soroban transaction loses its error type. No value is decoded wrongly (the issue states impact low).

entries.expected: the native value of Error(Storage, ExceededLimit) carries type storage and code exceeded_limit
entries.observed: Executed by the kit (the native error fact) on every JavaScript column: scValToNative gives {type: "system", code: 5, value: "scecExceededLimit"}, which carries the code and no error type; py-stellar-base 17.0.0 and 17.0.1 keep both.

entries.expected: the native value of Error(Budget, ExceededLimit) carries type budget and code exceeded_limit
entries.observed: Executed by the kit on every JavaScript column: the same native value as for Error(Storage, ExceededLimit).

evidence.pre_fix: make verify-conformance and the public set: on cap-0046/scval-error-storage-exceeded-limit and cap-0046/scval-error-budget-exceeded-limit (12-byte slices of diagnostic events of failed Soroban transactions, testnet ledger 5521432 and mainnet ledger 64558277), the native error fact diverges on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 16.4.1, 17.2.0, 17.2.1, 17.3.0 and 17.4.0: the native value carries no error type. The issue's script on 17.4.0 (16.4.1 and master 5243062 the same): both diagnostic events, copied from failed mainnet transactions, humanize to the same value, and all nine non-contract error types give the same output.
evidence.expected_basis: ScError is a union of ScErrorType and ScErrorCode (CAP-46, Stellar-contract.x); dropping the type loses which host subsystem failed.

reproduction.method: make verify-conformance OFFLINE=1 and xdrcheck conform run --set public: the native error fact diverges on every JavaScript column and conforms on both Python columns; re-run by hand on 2026-11-18 with the issue's two diagnostic events on 17.4.0.

history.note: Recorded on 2026-11-18: filed by the maintainers of this kit on 2026-11-14 as https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-sdk/issues/1905; this record restates the public issue.
Now executed by the kit: the driver protocol's native error fact (docs/conformance-protocol.md) on two error values sliced from network ledgers, both declaring it as a known divergence.
